title: Substitution in equality-free first-order sequent proofs

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)

summary: Rebuild equality-free quantified sequent certificates under weakening, free substitution and renaming, preserving proof height and protected parameters.
abstract: Replacing a name throughout a proof can fail if a quantified step accidentally binds part of its replacement term. We show how to perform the replacement on actual finite equality-free sequent proofs while keeping each newly chosen parameter separate from the surrounding formulas. The same construction enlarges the allowed alternatives and renames parameters, even when several old names receive the same image. Every transformed proof uses the original seven rules and has exactly the same height. Temporary witness names remain available in languages without constants, and a concrete two-element interpretation shows why capturing an inserted name would change the assertion.
